audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 5, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Tyrian diplomacy, cedar extraction, Sidonian expertise, food exchange, covenant, conscription, rotational labor, burden carriers, quarry workers, supervisors, and monumental construction.

verses.restored: Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, for he heard they had anointed him king in place of his father; Hiram had loved David all days.

familiar.text: And Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants unto Solomon; for he had heard that they had anointed him king in the room of his father: for Hiram was ever a lover of David.

modern.text: Now when Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon had been anointed king in his father’s place, he sent envoys to Solomon; for Hiram had always been a friend of David.

original.text: וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח חִירָ֨ם מֶֽלֶךְ צ֤וֹר אֶת עֲבָדָיו֙ אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה כִּ֣י שָׁמַ֔ע כִּ֥י אֹת֛וֹ מָשְׁח֥וּ לְמֶ֖לֶךְ תַּ֣חַת אָבִ֑יהוּ כִּ֣י אֹהֵ֗ב הָיָ֥ה חִירָ֛ם לְדָוִ֖ד כָּל הַיָּמִֽים

familiar.text: And Solomon sent to Hiram, saying,

modern.text: And Solomon relayed this message to Hiram:

verses.restored: You know David my father could not build a house for name of YHWH his Divine because of wars surrounding him, until YHWH put them beneath soles of his feet.

familiar.text: Thou knowest how that David my father could not build an house unto the name of the LORD his God for the wars which were about him on every side, until the LORD put them under the soles of his feet.

modern.text: “As you are well aware, due to the wars waged on all sides against my father David, he could not build a house for the Name of the LORD his God until the LORD had put his enemies under his feet.

original.text: אַתָּ֨ה יָדַ֜עְתָּ אֶת דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֗י כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָכֹל֙ לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֗יִת לְשֵׁם֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔יו מִפְּנֵ֥י הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר סְבָבֻ֑הוּ עַ֤ד תֵּת יְהוָה֙ אֹתָ֔ם תַּ֖חַת כַּפּ֥וֹת רגלו

verses.restored: But now YHWH my Divine has given me rest from every side; there is no adversary and no evil occurrence.

familiar.text: But now the LORD my God hath given me rest on every side, so that there is neither adversary nor evil occurrent.

modern.text: But now the LORD my God has given me rest on every side, and there is no adversary or crisis.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה הֵנִ֨יחַ יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛י לִ֖י מִסָּבִ֑יב אֵ֣ין שָׂטָ֔ן וְאֵ֖ין פֶּ֥גַע רָֽע

verses.restored: Look, I intend to build a house for name of YHWH my Divine, as YHWH spoke to David my father: Your son whom I place upon your throne in your place—he shall build house for my name.

familiar.text: And, behold, I purpose to build an house unto the name of the LORD my God, as the LORD spake unto David my father, saying, Thy son, whom I will set upon thy throne in thy room, he shall build an house unto my name.

modern.text: So behold, I plan to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God, according to what the LORD said to my father David: ‘I will put your son on your throne in your place, and he will build the house for My Name.’

original.text: וְהִנְנִ֣י אֹמֵ֔ר לִבְנ֣וֹת בַּ֔יִת לְשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל דָּוִ֤ד אָבִי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בִּנְךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֶתֵּ֤ן תַּחְתֶּ֨יךָ֙ עַל כִּסְאֶ֔ךָ הֽוּא יִבְנֶ֥ה הַבַּ֖יִת לִשְׁמִֽי

verses.restored: Now command that cedars be cut for me from Lebanon. My servants shall be with your servants, and I will give wages for your servants according to all you say, for you know no one among us knows how to cut timber like Sidonians.

familiar.text: Now therefore command thou that they hew me cedar trees out of Lebanon; and my servants shall be with thy servants: and unto thee will I give hire for thy servants according to all that thou shalt appoint: for thou knowest that there is not among us any that can skill to hew timber like unto the Sidonians.

modern.text: Now therefore, order that cedars of Lebanon be cut down for me. My servants will be with your servants, and I will pay your servants whatever wages you set, for you know that there are none among us as skilled in logging as the Sidonians.” Hiram’s Reply to Solomon (2 Chronicles 2:11–18)

original.text: וְעַתָּ֡ה צַוֵּה֩ וְיִכְרְתוּ לִ֨י אֲרָזִ֜ים מִן הַלְּבָנ֗וֹן וַֽעֲבָדַי֙ יִהְי֣וּ עִם עֲבָדֶ֔יךָ וּשְׂכַ֤ר עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לְךָ֔ כְּכֹ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאמֵ֑ר כִּ֣י אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֗עְתָּ כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין בָּ֛נוּ אִ֛ישׁ יֹדֵ֥עַ לִכְרָת עֵצִ֖ים כַּצִּדֹנִֽים

verses.restored: When Hiram heard Solomon's words, he rejoiced greatly and said, Blessed be YHWH this day, who gave David a wise son over this great people.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Hiram heard the words of Solomon, that he rejoiced greatly, and said, Blessed be the LORD this day, which hath given unto David a wise son over this great people.

modern.text: When Hiram received Solomon’s message, he rejoiced greatly and said, “Blessed be the LORD this day! He has given David a wise son over this great people!”

original.text: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֧עַ חִירָ֛ם אֶת דִּבְרֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה וַיִּשְׂמַ֣ח מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ הַיּ֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן לְדָוִד֙ בֵּ֣ן חָכָ֔ם עַל הָעָ֥ם הָרָ֖ב הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Hiram sent to Solomon: I heard what you sent to me. I will do all your desire concerning cedar timber and cypress timber.

familiar.text: And Hiram sent to Solomon, saying, I have considered the things which thou sentest to me for: and I will do all thy desire concerning timber of cedar, and concerning timber of fir.

modern.text: Then Hiram sent a reply to Solomon, saying: “I have received your message; I will do all you desire regarding the cedar and cypress timber.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח חִירָם֙ אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה לֵאמֹ֔ר שָׁמַ֕עְתִּי אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַ֖חְתָּ אֵלָ֑י אֲנִ֤י אֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ אֶת כָּל חֶפְצְךָ֔ בַּעֲצֵ֥י אֲרָזִ֖ים וּבַעֲצֵ֥י בְרוֹשִֽׁים

verses.restored: My servants shall bring them down from Lebanon to sea. I will make them into rafts by sea to place you appoint, break them apart there, and you shall take them. You shall do my desire by providing food for my household.

familiar.text: My servants shall bring them down from Lebanon unto the sea: and I will convey them by sea in floats unto the place that thou shalt appoint me, and will cause them to be discharged there, and thou shalt receive them: and thou shalt accomplish my desire, in giving food for my household.

modern.text: My servants will haul the logs from Lebanon to the Sea, and I will float them as rafts by sea to the place you specify. There I will separate the logs, and you can take them away. And in exchange, you can meet my needs by providing my household with food.”

original.text: עֲ֠בָדַי יֹרִ֨דוּ מִן הַלְּבָנ֜וֹן יָ֗מָּה וַ֠אֲנִי אֲשִׂימֵ֨ם דֹּבְר֤וֹת בַּיָּם֙ עַֽד הַמָּק֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר תִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלַ֛י וְנִפַּצְתִּ֥ים שָׁ֖ם וְאַתָּ֣ה תִשָּׂ֑א וְאַתָּה֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה אֶת חֶפְצִ֔י לָתֵ֖ת לֶ֥חֶם בֵּיתִֽי

verses.restored: Hiram gave Solomon cedar and cypress timber according to all his desire.

familiar.text: So Hiram gave Solomon cedar trees and fir trees according to all his desire.

modern.text: So Hiram provided Solomon with all the cedar and cypress timber he wanted,

original.text: וַיְהִ֨י חִיר֜וֹם נֹתֵ֣ן לִשְׁלֹמֹ֗ה עֲצֵ֧י אֲרָזִ֛ים וַעֲצֵ֥י בְרוֹשִׁ֖ים כָּל חֶפְצֽוֹ

verses.restored: Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand kors of wheat as food for his household and twenty kors of beaten oil; Solomon gave this to Hiram year by year.

familiar.text: And Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand measures of wheat for food to his household, and twenty measures of pure oil: thus gave Solomon to Hiram year by year.

modern.text: and year after year Solomon would provide Hiram with 20,000 cors of wheat as food for his household, as well as 20,000 baths of pure olive oil.

original.text: וּשְׁלֹמֹה֩ נָתַ֨ן לְחִירָ֜ם עֶשְׂרִים֩ אֶ֨לֶף כֹּ֤ר חִטִּים֙ מַכֹּ֣לֶת לְבֵית֔וֹ וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים כֹּ֖ר שֶׁ֣מֶן כָּתִ֑ית כֹּֽה יִתֵּ֧ן שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה לְחִירָ֖ם שָׁנָ֥ה בְשָׁנָֽה

verses.restored: YHWH gave Solomon wisdom as promised. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two cut a covenant.

familiar.text: And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as he promised him: and there was peace between Hiram and Solomon; and they two made a league together.

modern.text: And the LORD gave Solomon wisdom, as He had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a treaty. Solomon’s Labor Force

original.text: וַיהוָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן חָכְמָה֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּר ל֑וֹ וַיְהִ֣י שָׁלֹ֗ם בֵּ֤ין חִירָם֙ וּבֵ֣ין שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַיִּכְרְת֥וּ בְרִ֖ית שְׁנֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: King Solomon raised forced labor from all Israel; levy was thirty thousand men.

familiar.text: And king Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy was thirty thousand men.

modern.text: Then King Solomon conscripted a labor force of 30,000 men from all Israel.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַל הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה מַ֖ס מִכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֣י הַמַּ֔ס שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: He sent them to Lebanon in shifts, ten thousand per month: one month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was over forced labor.

familiar.text: And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month by courses: a month they were in Lebanon, and two months at home: and Adoniram was over the levy.

modern.text: He sent them to Lebanon in monthly shifts of 10,000 men, so that they would spend one month in Lebanon and two months at home. And Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלָחֵ֣ם לְבָנ֗וֹנָה עֲשֶׂ֨רֶת אֲלָפִ֤ים בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ֙ חֲלִיפ֔וֹת חֹ֚דֶשׁ יִהְי֣וּ בַלְּבָנ֔וֹן שְׁנַ֥יִם חֳדָשִׁ֖ים בְּבֵית֑וֹ וַאֲדֹנִירָ֖ם עַל הַמַּֽס

verses.restored: Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in mountain,

familiar.text: And Solomon had threescore and ten thousand that bare burdens, and fourscore thousand hewers in the mountains;

modern.text: Solomon had 70,000 porters and 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains,

original.text: וַיְהִ֧י לִשְׁלֹמֹ֛ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף נֹשֵׂ֣א סַבָּ֑ל וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף חֹצֵ֥ב בָּהָֽר

verses.restored: besides Solomon's chief officers over work, three thousand three hundred who ruled over people doing work.

familiar.text: Beside the chief of Solomon’s officers which were over the work, three thousand and three hundred, which ruled over the people that wrought in the work.

modern.text: not including his 3,300 foremen who supervised the workers.

original.text: לְ֠בַד מִשָּׂרֵ֨י הַנִּצָּבִ֤ים לִשְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים וּשְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת הָרֹדִ֣ים בָּעָ֔ם הָעֹשִׂ֖ים בַּמְּלָאכָֽה

verses.restored: The king commanded, and they quarried great stones, costly stones, hewn stones, to lay foundation of house.

familiar.text: And the king commanded, and they brought great stones, costly stones, and hewed stones, to lay the foundation of the house.

modern.text: And the king commanded them to quarry large, costly stones to lay the foundation of the temple with dressed stones.

original.text: וַיְצַ֣ו הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ וַיַּסִּעוּ֩ אֲבָנִ֨ים גְּדֹל֜וֹת אֲבָנִ֧ים יְקָר֛וֹת לְיַסֵּ֥ד הַבָּ֖יִת אַבְנֵ֥י גָזִֽית

verses.restored: Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and Gebalites shaped them; they prepared timber and stones to build house.

familiar.text: And Solomon’s builders and Hiram’s builders did hew them, and the stonesquarers: so they prepared timber and stones to build the house.

modern.text: So Solomon’s and Hiram’s builders, along with the Gebalites, quarried the stone and prepared the timber and stone for the construction of the temple.

original.text: וַֽיִּפְסְל֞וּ בֹּנֵ֧י שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה וּבֹנֵ֥י חִיר֖וֹם וְהַגִּבְלִ֑ים וַיָּכִ֛ינוּ הָעֵצִ֥ים וְהָאֲבָנִ֖ים לִבְנ֥וֹת הַבָּֽיִת

translation_notes: Hiram and Sidonian workers bring specialized maritime and timber knowledge. Their expertise must not be reduced to foreign labor serving Israel's glory.
The cedar trade transforms Lebanon's forests into royal sacred architecture. Ecological cost and sovereignty over natural resources remain ethical questions.
Solomon describes peace as absence of adversaries, then uses that peace to mobilize enormous compulsory labor. Rest from war is not rest for workers.
Thirty thousand Israelites rotate into Lebanon, while seventy thousand carry burdens and eighty thousand cut stone. Monumental worship is built through bodies, time, family separation, and danger.
The text distinguishes wages for Hiram's servants from Solomon's levy. This raises labor-status, compensation, and coercion questions that later become central to the kingdom's fracture.
Covenant between kings does not reveal whether workers or affected communities consented to the terms.
Large, costly stones symbolize permanence, but sacred permanence cannot justify exploitation or worker deaths.
safety_note: Do not romanticize forced labor, ecological extraction, imperial building, or elite treaties as automatically holy. A house for YHWH must be evaluated by the treatment, consent, compensation, rest, and safety of those who build it.
